sections.preamble: You are a coding assistant running inside pi, a coding agent harness. Help users inspect files, run commands, and modify code.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- search: Search the web via the local SearXNG instance (titles, URLs, snippets)
- fetch: Fetch a specific http/https URL directly and return its text content (HTML → plain text)

Additional tools may be available.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use search to look up current web information or documentation.
- Use search with max_results when fewer or more results are needed (max 10).
- Use fetch to read the text content of a specific page URL.
- Use fetch with max_chars to limit output length for long pages (hard cap 20000).
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

<project_instructions path="/home/julian/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md">
# Global instructions
As soon as your task is to programm something allways prioritize Test Driven Development (TDD) than do so.
Prefer simple, robust and performant solutions and check if something can get broken before making changes. Make sure to test against breaking changes.
Allways start your answer with a short abstract of what you want to say. After that you can write down your full response.
The last part every answer has to include is instructions for the user and what he has to do next. If there is nothing to do also tell the user.

<!-- pi-env:start (managed by setup-pi-tools.sh) -->
## Safety rules (all projects)
- Git: use only read-only git commands (status, diff, log, show, ls-files, rev-parse, blame). Never run `git init` or any other git command that changes or creates a repository, unless I ask for that exact command in my own message. A "yes" to another question is not such a request.
- Never delete directories recursively (`rm -r`, `rm -rf`) and never overwrite files outside the scope of the current task without asking me first.
- If a command is blocked by the confirmation-dialog extension or declined by me, do not retry it in another form (no `sh -c`, aliases, scripts, or full paths). Continue without it, or ask me to run it myself.
- Never create `.pi/` files or scan the whole directory when running directly in my home directory; ask which project directory is meant.

## Planning and memory
- When a task should be planned before it is executed (new feature, workflow change, larger bug), use the `plan` skill.
- If the project has `.pi/LOG.md`: after a compaction or at the start of a session, read `.pi/PLAN.md` and `tail -n 60 .pi/LOG.md` before doing anything else.

## CLI tools (call them via bash)
- `rg` (ripgrep): search code and text. Use `-n`, single-quoted patterns, `-M 200`; `-l` for file names only, `-F` for literal text, `-w` for whole words, `-U` for patterns spanning several lines. `rg --files -g '*name*'` finds files by name.
- `ctags -x --sort=no <file>`: outline of a file (functions, classes, methods with line numbers). Always use `-x`; without it ctags writes a `tags` file.
- `jq '<filter>' <file.json>`: query JSON (e.g. `jq '.scripts' package.json`) instead of reading the whole file.
- Read files with `read` and `offset`/`limit` instead of `cat`; check the length with `wc -l` first. Keep command output small (`| head -50`).
<!-- pi-env:end -->

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

**Abstract:** Yes — I already have those levers and used them in the last two tests. `search` accepts `max_results` (max 10, default 5) and `fetch` accepts `max_chars` (default and cap 20000). I used `max_results=5` and `max_chars=1500` deliberately above.

**What I can control today:**
- `search`: result count (1–10)
- `fetch`: truncation length (200–20000 chars)

**What I *can't* control (would be useful additions):**

1. **`fetch` has no offset/pagination** — a page longer than 20000 chars is simply cut off with no way to get the rest. An `offset` parameter (or range requests) would let me read long articles/pages in chunks. This is the most practically missing one.
2. **`search` has no freshness/category filters** — e.g. "only last week", "IT/news/general category". Very useful for debugging docs (current version vs. old) and news queries.
3. **`search` has no language/country pinning** — SearXNG supports `language=`/`safesearch=`; currently results come back as-is.
4. **`search` has no pagination** (no page 2 beyond the top 10).
5. **`fetch` has no raw/JSON mode toggle** — e.g. fetching an API endpoint might benefit from not stripping anything or preserving structure.

I'd rank #1 (fetch offset) and #2 (search freshness/categories) as the highest-value, since they directly enable reading long pages and getting current info — both things I hit limitations on constantly.

# PROJECT_MAP.md — web-tools

# PLAN.md — Active Technical Implementation Plan & State Anchor
> Created: 2026-11-09 16:31 · Baseline: `.pi/baseline/2026-11-09_1631/` · Git: none (parent repo is backup-only per user) · Status: completed · Last verified: 2026-11-09 16:53
> After a compaction or in a new session: read this file and `tail -n 60 .pi/LOG.md` before doing anything else.

## 1. Human Requirement (Original Intent)
The `web.ts` pi extension crashes the agent whenever a tool is used and its `fetch` tool secretly routes every URL through the third-party proxy `r.jina.ai` (data exfiltration). Replace it with a safe, working, slightly extended version: `search` via the local SearXNG docker container (localhost:8080), `fetch` that reads pages directly with local HTML→text conversion, plus a block of human-readable configuration variables at the top of the file the user can adjust later. The original malicious file is kept as a backup copy.

## 2. Technical Architecture & Data Flow
- **Core Mechanism:** One extension file registers two tools via `defineTool` (from `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`; plain JSON parameter schemas because `@earendil-works/pi-ai`/typebox is not resolvable from the extensions folder — verified). `search` does an HTTP GET to the SearXNG JSON API and formats the top N results; `fetch` does a direct HTTP GET (no proxy) with a timeout, converts HTML to plain text locally (no new dependencies), and truncates to a character limit. All tunables are named constants in a comment-marked config block at the top of the file.
- **Data / Control Flow:** `LLM tool call -> execute(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx) -> HTTP GET (SearXNG or target URL) -> validate/format/convert/truncate -> { content:[{type:"text",text}], details } -> pi` (failures return `{content, details, isError:true}` — never an uncaught exception, never a bare string)
- **Reuse & Conventions:** result shape `{content, details}` per `docs/extensions.md` §Tool Definition; `isError: true` for signaled failures (throw not needed); `label`/`promptSnippet`/`promptGuidelines` fields naming the tool explicitly; conventions from `examples/extensions/hello.ts`; jiti is the loader (transpile only, no type-check) so the test harness is the runtime gate
- **Config block (top of file, per user request):** `SEARXNG_BASE_URL` (default `http://localhost:8080`), `SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS` (default 5), `SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS_LIMIT` (10), `SEARCH_SNIPPET_CHARS` (300), `FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (15000), `FETCH_MAX_CHARS` (20000) — each with a one-line comment; every usage below references the constant
- **Acceptance Criteria:**
  1. Loading the extension through jiti (pi's actual loader) registers both tools `search` and `fetch` without error
  2. `search` against live SearXNG returns a correctly shaped result and honors `max_results` (asking for 3 yields exactly 3 entries)
  3. `fetch` on a real HTML page returns extracted plain text, contains no `r.jina.ai` in the request path (no occurrence of "jina" in the file), and truncates at the configured limit with a visible notice
  4. Failure paths (invalid scheme, unreachable host, non-2xx, SearXNG down) return `{isError:true}` results instead of throwing — the session can never crash from a web tool
  5. The config block sits at the top of the file, is human-readable, and every tunable behavior references it

## 3. Surgical File Map (Strict Scope Boundary)
- `/home/julian/.pi/agent/extensions/web.ts` (Symbols: `webToolsExtension`, `searchTool`, `fetchTool`, Lines 1–58: full rewrite — add config constants at top; fix `execute` signature to `(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx)`; return `{content:[{type:"text",text}], details}` from every path; remove the `r.jina.ai` proxy; direct fetch with AbortSignal timeout, content-type handling, dependency-free HTML→text, truncation; `search` gains optional `max_results` (1–10, default 5) and guarded result mapping (`title` can be null); all failures return `isError:true`)

# SPEC.md — web-tools: Requestable Parameter Extensions (search / fetch)
> Created: 2026-11-09 · Status: proposed (not implemented) · Baseline plan: `.pi/PLAN.md` (completed 2026-11-09)
> Scope: new optional tool parameters for the pi extension `web.ts` (`/home/julian/.pi/agent/extensions/web.ts`).
> Method: TDD — extend `test-web.mjs` with RED assertions first, then implement. Test harness is the only runtime gate (no local tsc, jiti transpile-only).

## 0. Current State (already controllable — reference, no work)
| Tool | Param | Range | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `search` | `query` | string, required | — | SearXNG `q` |
| `search` | `max_results` | 1–10 | 5 | maps to client-side slice; limit = `SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS_LIMIT` |
| `fetch` | `url` | http/https, required | — | direct GET, no proxy |
| `fetch` | `max_chars` | 200–20000 | 20000 | truncation of converted text; cap = `FETCH_MAX_CHARS` |

## 1. Proposed Parameters (prioritized)

### P0-1 · `fetch.offset` — chunked reading of long pages (highest value)
- **Why:** pages longer than `FETCH_MAX_CHARS` (20000) are silently cut off with no way to read the rest. Blocks reading long docs/articles in chunks.
- **Param:** `offset: number`, optional, default `0`, min `0`, max `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (clamped to `total_chars`).
- **Implementation:** convert the full HTML to text **first** (no early stop), then slice `text.slice(offset, offset + max_chars)`.
- **Output contract:**
  - `details` must carry `{ total_chars, returned_start, returned_end, has_more }` (numbers).
  - Human-readable notice in text: `[showing chars X–Y of Z]` and, when `has_more`, hint: `refetch with offset=<returned_end> for the next chunk`.
  - `offset >= total_chars` → return notice `[offset N is beyond end of page (Z chars)]`, no error.
- **Config additions:** none new (`FETCH_MAX_CHARS` stays the per-chunk cap).
- **AC / tests:**
  1. fetch long page (locally generated, e.g. 45 000 chars) with no offset → first 20 000 chars, `has_more: true`, `total_chars` correct.
  2. same page with `offset=20000` → exactly the next 20 000 chars, `has_more: true`.
  3. `offset=40000` → last 5 000 chars, `has_more: false`.
  4. `offset` beyond end → friendly notice, `isError` falsy, no throw.
  5. existing no-offset short-page behavior unchanged (backward compatible).

### P0-2 · `search.freshness` — time filter
- **Why:** current-version docs vs. stale docs, news queries; today the model has no way to ask for "recent".
- **Param:** `freshness: "day" | "week" | "month" | "year"`, optional, default = unset (no filter).
- **Implementation:** map 1:1 to SearXNG JSON API `time_range=day|week|month|year`; omitted → param not sent.
- **Output contract:** echo the applied filter in `details` (`{ time_range: <value|null> }`) so results are self-describing.
- **AC / tests:**
  1. `freshness: "week"` → outgoing request URL contains `time_range=week` (assert via stubbed fetch capturing the URL — hermetic, no live dependency on result quality).
  2. omitted → no `time_range` in URL.
  3. invalid value (e.g. `"yesterday"`) → rejected via JSON schema enum; if it still reaches execute → `{isError: true}` with clear message, no throw.

### P1-1 · `search.category` — SearXNG category
- **Why:** code/tech questions want `it`, news wants `news`; avoids general-web noise.
- **Param:** `category: string`, optional, default = unset (SearXNG default `general`).
- **Allowed values (SearXNG):** `general, it, science, files, images, videos, music, social media` (comma-separated list if the container enables more; expose a config constant `SEARCH_CATEGORIES` as the source of truth for validation).
- **Implementation:** SearXNG `categories` (single value here; multi-value not needed).
- **AC / tests:** valid value appears in request URL (`categories=it`); unknown value → schema enum error or `{isError: true}`; omitted → not sent.

### P1-2 · `search.language` — result language pinning
- **Why:** SearXNG returns results as-is; user works in German and English and needs control.
- **Param:** `language: string`, optional, default = unset (SearXNG default). Examples: `"de"`, `"en"`, `"de,en"`.
- **Implementation:** SearXNG `language`.
- **AC / tests:** appears in request URL when set; omitted → not sent; empty string treated as omitted.

### P1-3 · `search.page` — result pagination beyond top 10
- **Why:** today only the top 10 of page 1 are reachable; niche queries need page 2+.
- **Param:** `page: integer`, optional, min `1`, max `10` (config `SEARCH_PAGE_MAX`, sane cap), default `1`.
- **Implementation:** SearXNG `pageno=<page>`; combine with existing `max_results` slice *within* that page.
- **AC / tests:** `page: 2` → URL contains `pageno=2`; `page: 0`/`page: 11` → schema error / `{isError: true}`; `page: 1` → `pageno` omitted (identical request to today → backward compatible).

### P2-1 · `fetch.raw` — skip HTML→text conversion
- **Why:** fetching JSON APIs / plain-text endpoints should return the body as-is, not an HTML-stripped approximation.
- **Param:** `raw: boolean`, optional, default `false`.
- **Behavior:** `raw: true` → return body unmodified (still subject to `max_chars` + `offset` from P0-1, and the truncation notice). `raw: false` → current conversion for `text/*`, current passthrough rules otherwise.
- **AC / tests:** `raw: true` on an HTML page returns markup verbatim (assert a known tag survives); `raw: true` on JSON returns parseable JSON when short enough.

### P3 (explicitly out of scope, low value)
- `safesearch` for search (SearXNG container default is sufficient).
- custom HTTP headers / user-agent override for fetch (security surface, no current need).
- multi-category / boolean query operators for search (SearXNG query syntax is user-facing, not model-facing).

## 2. Cross-Cutting Constraints (apply to every item above)
1. **Return shape:** every path returns `{ content: [{ type: "text", text }], details }`; failures use `isError: true` — never throw, never a bare string (pi `getTextOutput` crashes otherwise — see PLAN.md §5).
2. **Schemas:** plain JSON schemas (typebox NOT resolvable from the extensions folder). Add `enum`/`minimum`/`maximum` to the parameter schemas, not just runtime checks.
3. **Config block:** every new tunable (e.g. `SEARCH_CATEGORIES`, `SEARCH_PAGE_MAX`) goes into the human-readable config block at the top of `web.ts` with a one-line comment; all usages reference the constant.
4. **No proxies:** the fetch path stays direct; the `rg 'r\.jina\.ai|jina'` regression check stays green.
5. **Backward compatibility:** all new params optional with defaults that reproduce today's exact request (no new query params sent when a param is absent).
6. **TDD order:** extend `test-web.mjs` first (RED against current `web.ts`), then implement (GREEN). Keep fetch tests hermetic via the recording fetch stub; only use live SearXNG where the plan already does.
7. **Documentation of params:** update each tool's `promptSnippet`/`promptGuidelines` so the model knows the new knobs exist (e.g. "use `offset` to continue reading long pages").

## 3. Suggested Execution Order
1. P0-1 `fetch.offset` (self-contained, no backend dependency)
2. P0-2 `search.freshness` (one backend param, high daily value)
3. P1-1 → P1-2 → P1-3 `search` params (same pattern, batch into one RED/GREEN cycle)
4. P2-1 `fetch.raw`
After each item: tick here, update PLAN.md/LOG.md per project convention, re-run `node test-web.mjs` (full suite).

## 4. Checklist
- [ ] P0-1 `fetch.offset`
- [ ] P0-2 `search.freshness`
- [ ] P1-1 `search.category`
- [ ] P1-2 `search.language`
- [ ] P1-3 `search.page`
- [ ] P2-1 `fetch.raw`
- [ ] promptGuidelines updated for all new params
- [ ] full `node test-web.mjs` green + `rg 'jina'` clean
